analysis:
The code snippet contains a call to the `get` method of a List: `ability.getCosts().get(0)`. According to the API documentation, `List.get(int index)` throws `IndexOutOfBoundsException` if the index is out of range (i.e., index < 0 or index >= size()). In the snippet, this call appears in a compound condition: 
- First use: `!ability.getTargets().isEmpty() || !(ability.getCosts().size() == 1 && ability.getCosts().get(0) instanceof SacrificeSourceCost) || ...` 
- Second use: `!(ability.getCosts().size() == 2 && ability.getCosts().get(0) instanceof TapSourceCost && ability.getCosts().get(0) instanceof SacrificeSourceCost)`
In both cases, the size of the list is explicitly checked (`size() == 1` or `size() == 2`) before calling `get(0)`. This ensures that the list has at least one element, so the index 0 is always valid. Therefore, the `IndexOutOfBoundsException` condition is fully avoided by these guard checks.
